title: Efficacy of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome vaccines in animal models: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis that threatens both animal and human health across East Asia, yet no licensed vaccine is currently available. We therefore conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of preclinical murine and ferret studies to evaluate severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus vaccine efficacy. Seven electronic databases were searched for studies published between 2009 and 2025. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated mortality, viremia, and post-challenge weight loss. Quantitative viral burden was further evaluated using standardized mean differences for mean and peak viremia, whereas body-weight trajectories were assessed using generalized linear mixed models. Twenty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was attenuated in the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis (RR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.36–1.51). Furthermore, significantly suppressing both mean and peak viremia under homologous and heterologous challenge conditions. Longitudinal analyses further demonstrated improved preservation of body weight, particularly following mRNA and vector vaccination. These findings provide the strongest quantitative evidence supporting the development of broadly protective SFTSV vaccines for both human and veterinary use within a One Health framework.

title: Development of anti-Gn monoclonal antibodies for magnetic nanoparticle-coupled lateral flow detection of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus
abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging tick-borne zoonotic pathogen associated with high mortality in humans and silent circulation in animals, highlighting the need for rapid, field-deployable diagnostics. Current molecular and serological methods remain dependent on specialized infrastructure, limiting their use in resource-limited settings. Here, we developed a magnetic nanoparticle-enhanced lateral flow assay targeting the SFTSV glycoprotein Gn (Gn-LFA) for rapid antigen detection. A panel of anti-Gn monoclonal antibodies was generated and systematically characterized for isotype, epitope recognition, binding affinity, and viral capture efficiency. A monoclonal antibody exhibiting strong Gn recognition and antigen-capturing activity was selected as the detection antibody and conjugated to magnetic nanoparticles, while three additional antibodies were used as capture antibodies on the test line to improve antigen recognition. The Gn-LFA detected recombinant Gn proteins produced in both mammalian and plant expression systems and demonstrated compatibility across sera from multiple host species. The assay detected as little as 20 ng of recombinant Gn protein or approximately 5 × 10 5 FFU of SFTSV within 45 min without requiring specialized instrumentation. Collectively, this study provides proof of concept for a rapid and low-cost approach to SFTSV antigen detection and supports its further development for potential applications in resource-limited settings and One Health surveillance.

title_zh: 针对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)的抗Gn单克隆抗体开发用于磁性纳米粒子偶联侧向流动检测
source_body_en: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging tick-borne zoonotic pathogen associated with high mortality in humans and silent circulation in animals, highlighting the need for rapid, field-deployable diagnostics. Current molecular and serological methods remain dependent on specialized infrastructure, limiting their use in resource-limited settings. Here, we developed a magnetic nanoparticle-enhanced lateral flow assay targeting the SFTSV glycoprotein Gn (Gn-LFA) for rapid antigen detection. A panel of anti-Gn monoclonal antibodies was generated and systematically characterized for isotype, epitope recognition, binding affinity, and viral capture efficiency. A monoclonal antibody exhibiting strong Gn recognition and antigen-capturing activity was selected as the detection antibody and conjugated to magnetic nanoparticles, while three additional antibodies were used as capture antibodies on the test line to improve antigen recognition. The Gn-LFA detected recombinant Gn proteins produced in both mammalian and plant expression systems and demonstrated compatibility across sera from multiple host species. The assay detected as little as 20 ng of recombinant Gn protein or approximately 5 × 10 5 FFU of SFTSV within 45 min without requiring specialized instrumentation. Collectively, this study provides proof of concept for a rapid and low-cost approach to SFTSV antigen detection and supports its further development for potential applications in resource-limited settings and One Health surveillance.

title: Systematic review and meta-regression analysis of the prevalence of Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in humans, ticks and animals in Sub-Saharan Africa from 1980 to 2025
abstract: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is an emerging infectious tick-borne virus that continues to impact public health globally. To re-evaluate and improve CCHFV control strategies in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), there’s a need to aggregate CCHFV prevalence data and explore the factors which affect observed variations in prevalence in humans, animals and ticks. Articles reporting prevalence of CCHFV in humans, animals and ticks in SSA between 1980 and 2025 were retrieved from five research databases, namely: Scopus, PubMed, Springer Nature, Web of Science and Science Direct. A random effects model was fit using a binomial generalised linear mixed effects model with a logit link to estimate pooled prevalences for each host species, along with their 95% confidence intervals. title: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling characterizes tryptophan metabolic disturbance associated with mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients
abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is associated with high mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients; however, the integrated proteomic–metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes remain poorly characterized. This prospective cohort study enrolled 68 patients with SFTS, who were admitted to the ICU and classified them as survivors (n = 33) or non-survivors (n = 35) according to their 28-day clinical outcomes. Untargeted metabolomic profiling using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry and quantitative proteomic profiling using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry were performed on plasma samples collected at ICU admission. Multivariable analysis, pathway enrichment analysis, correlation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to identify potential prognostic biomarkers and characterize molecular associations. Non-survivors exhibited more severe multi-organ injury and systemic inflammation. Metabolomic profiling revealed marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism: L-tryptophan levels were decreased, whereas kynurenine and its downstream metabolites (kynurenic acid [KA], 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid [3-HAA], xanthurenic acid [XA], and 5-hydroxyindolepyruvate [5-HIP]) were increased, suggesting activation of the kynurenine pathway. The four core tryptophan metabolites yielded a combined area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 for predicting 28-day mortality and were correlated with indicators of renal function and coagulation. Proteomic profiling identified 200 differentially expressed proteins: proteins upregulated in survivors were enriched in the proteasome pathway, whereas those upregulated in non-survivors were enriched in the IL-17 pathway and other inflammatory and immune pathways. Integrated analysis revealed that the four tryptophan metabolites were associated with 20 differentially expressed proteins, six of which showed robust associations within outcome subgroups. Collectively, tryptophan metabolic disturbances coupled with inflammatory proteomic features may characterize fatal severe SFTS, and the identified metabolite–protein signatures may serve as promising prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in critically ill patients.

title_zh: 整合蛋白质组学和代谢组学分析揭示与ICU收治发热伴血小板减少综合征患者相关的色氨酸代谢紊乱
source_body_en: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is associated with high mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients; however, the integrated proteomic–metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes remain poorly characterized. This prospective cohort study enrolled 68 patients with SFTS, who were admitted to the ICU and classified them as survivors (n = 33) or non-survivors (n = 35) according to their 28-day clinical outcomes. Untargeted metabolomic profiling using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry and quantitative proteomic profiling using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry were performed on plasma samples collected at ICU admission. Multivariable analysis, pathway enrichment analysis, correlation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to identify potential prognostic biomarkers and characterize molecular associations. Non-survivors exhibited more severe multi-organ injury and systemic inflammation. Metabolomic profiling revealed marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism: L-tryptophan levels were decreased, whereas kynurenine and its downstream metabolites (kynurenic acid [KA], 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid [3-HAA], xanthurenic acid [XA], and 5-hydroxyindolepyruvate [5-HIP]) were increased, suggesting activation of the kynurenine pathway. The four core tryptophan metabolites yielded a combined area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 for predicting 28-day mortality and were correlated with indicators of renal function and coagulation. Proteomic profiling identified 200 differentially expressed proteins: proteins upregulated in survivors were enriched in the proteasome pathway, whereas those upregulated in non-survivors were enriched in the IL-17 pathway and other inflammatory and immune pathways. Integrated analysis revealed that the four tryptophan metabolites were associated with 20 differentially expressed proteins, six of which showed robust associations within outcome subgroups. Collectively, tryptophan metabolic disturbances coupled with inflammatory proteomic features may characterize fatal severe SFTS, and the identified metabolite–protein signatures may serve as promising prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in critically ill patients.
abstract_zh: 由大别山布尼亚病毒引起的发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)与重症监护病房(ICU)患者高死亡率相关;然而,导致致命结局的整合蛋白质组学-代谢组学机制仍不明确。本前瞻性发热伴血小板减少综合征研究纳入了68名因发热伴血小板减少综合征而入住ICU的患者,并根据其28天的临床结局将其分为幸存者(n=33)和非幸存者(n=35)。采用超高效液相色谱-串联质谱法对ICU入院时采集的血浆样本进行非靶向代谢组学分析,并采用数据非依赖采集质谱法进行定量蛋白质组学分析。通过多变量分析、通路富集分析、相关性分析和受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析,识别潜在的预后生物标志物并阐明分子关联。非幸存者表现出更严重的多器官损伤和全身性炎症。代谢组学分析显示色氨酸代谢显著紊乱:L-色氨酸水平降低,而色氨酮及其下游代谢产物(色氨酮酸[KA]、3-羟基邻氨基苯甲酸[3-HAA]、黄尿酸[XA]和5-羟基吲哚乙酸[5-HIP])水平升高,提示色氨酮通路被激活。四种核心色氨酸代谢产物在预测28天死亡率时的综合曲线下面积(AUC)为0.934,并与肾功能和凝血指标相关。蛋白质组学分析鉴定了200种差异表达蛋白:幸存者中上调的蛋白富集于蛋白酶体通路,而非幸存者中上调的蛋白则富集于IL-17通路及其他炎症和免疫通路。整合分析显示,这四种色氨酸代谢产物与20种差异表达蛋白相关,其中六种在结局亚组中表现出显著关联。总体而言,色氨酸代谢紊乱与炎症蛋白质组学特征相结合可能表征致命性发热伴血小板减少综合征,所鉴定的代谢物-蛋白特征可能成为危重患者预后生物标志物和潜在治疗靶点。

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A PCR TEST SYSTEM FOR THE GENETIC DIAGNOSIS OF HEMORRHAGIC FEVER WITH RENAL SYNDROME
abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is an acute zoonotic disease caused by orthohantaviruses. Reliable molecular diagnostics are essential for early detection and epizootiological surveillance. This study aimed to develop and validate a reverse transcription quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) assay for detection of HFRS-associated orthohantavirus RNA.Species-specific primers (HV P1-F and HV P1-R) and a TaqMan probe (HV P1) targeting the nucleocapsid protein (N) gene within the S segment were designed. A plasmid positive control containing a 242-bp target fragment was constructed. Analytical sensitivity, specificity, reproducibility, and repeatability were evaluated. Field testing included samples from 343 small mammals collected in endemic areas of the West Kazakhstan Region. The assay consistently detected the plasmid control from 1 ng/μL to 1 fg/μL, with Ct values of 37.35 and 37.73 at 1 fg/μL. No specific amplification was observed at 100 ag/μL. A strong linear relationship between Ct values and template concentration was obtained (R2 = 0.998). No false-positive reactions occurred with tick-borne encephalitis virus or Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus RNA. Reproducibility and repeatability showed 100% concordance of qualitative results. HFRS-associated orthohantavirus RNA was detected in 45 of 123 pooled field samples. The minimum infection prevalence was 13.1%, reaching 15.3% in Myodes glareolus and 13.3% in Apodemus uralensis and Microtus arvalis. The developed one-step RT-qPCR assay demonstrated high sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility and is suitable for routine diagnostics and surveillance of natural HFRS foci.

title: Cleavage-gated Cas13-to-DNA nanostructure transduction for target-preamplification-free viral RNA detection
abstract: CRISPR-Cas13a enables programmable RNA recognition without target nucleic-acid preamplification, but conventional assays encode collateral RNase activity by cleaving fluorescent reporters. Here, we developed a cleavage-gated strategy that converts transient Cas13a cleavage into a sequence-defined, strand-displacement-competent DNA actuator, shifting signal encoding from cumulative reporter intensity to a discrete scaffold topology. A chimeric masking hairpin (CMH) links Cas13a to a DNA nanostructure sensor (DNA-NS) by using a cleavable RNA loop to constrain a DNA-key bearing a pre-exposed toehold. Target-activated Cas13a cleaves the loop, converting the partially masked key into a strand-displacement-competent intermediate that reconfigures an M13mp18 scaffold from a linear to a looped state, producing a distinct electrophoretic mobility signature. Screening of 40 CMH-sensor-handle combinations identified a 4-nt toehold paired with an 18-nt sensor handle as the best-performing configuration within the tested design space (component-level ΔΔG = -1.19 kcal/mol at 37 °C). Using pooled crRNAs targeting the S, M, and L genomic segments of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), the assay detected the lowest tested input concentration of 10.38 fM in all three replicates. In a retrospective case-control evaluation of 87 plasma-derived RNA samples, the assay agreed with RT-qPCR for 45 of 47 positive specimens and 40 healthy controls, yielding a positive percent agreement of 95.7% and a negative percent agreement of 100%. Replacing the crRNAs redirected recognition to Hantaan virus reference RNA without redesigning the CMH or DNA-NS. This work establishes a modular framework for topology-resolved viral RNA detection without target preamplification.

title_zh: 基于裂解调控的Cas13a与DNA纳米结构转导技术实现无需靶标预扩增的病毒RNA检测
source_body_en: CRISPR-Cas13a enables programmable RNA recognition without target nucleic-acid preamplification, but conventional assays encode collateral RNase activity by cleaving fluorescent reporters. Here, we developed a cleavage-gated strategy that converts transient Cas13a cleavage into a sequence-defined, strand-displacement-competent DNA actuator, shifting signal encoding from cumulative reporter intensity to a discrete scaffold topology. A chimeric masking hairpin (CMH) links Cas13a to a DNA nanostructure sensor (DNA-NS) by using a cleavable RNA loop to constrain a DNA-key bearing a pre-exposed toehold. Target-activated Cas13a cleaves the loop, converting the partially masked key into a strand-displacement-competent intermediate that reconfigures an M13mp18 scaffold from a linear to a looped state, producing a distinct electrophoretic mobility signature. Screening of 40 CMH-sensor-handle combinations identified a 4-nt toehold paired with an 18-nt sensor handle as the best-performing configuration within the tested design space (component-level ΔΔG = -1.19 kcal/mol at 37 °C). Using pooled crRNAs targeting the S, M, and L genomic segments of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), the assay detected the lowest tested input concentration of 10.38 fM in all three replicates. In a retrospective case-control evaluation of 87 plasma-derived RNA samples, the assay agreed with RT-qPCR for 45 of 47 positive specimens and 40 healthy controls, yielding a positive percent agreement of 95.7% and a negative percent agreement of 100%. Replacing the crRNAs redirected recognition to Hantaan virus reference RNA without redesigning the CMH or DNA-NS. This work establishes a modular framework for topology-resolved viral RNA detection without target preamplification.
abstract_zh: CRISPR-Cas13a能够在不进行靶标核酸预扩增的情况下实现可编程的RNA识别,但传统检测方法通过裂解荧光报告分子来编码旁观者RNase活性。在这里,我们开发了一种裂解调控策略,将Cas13a的瞬时裂解转化为一种序列定义、能够进行链置换的DNA执行器,将信号编码从累积报告分子强度转移到离散的支架拓扑结构。一种嵌合掩蔽发夹(CMH)通过一个可裂解的RNA环将Cas13a与DNA纳米结构传感器(DNA-NS)连接起来,该环限制了一个带有预暴露脚手架的DNA密钥。当靶标激活Cas13a时,它会裂解该环,将部分掩蔽的密钥转化为能够进行链置换的中间体,从而重新配置M13mp18支架从线性状态转变为环状状态,产生独特的电泳迁移率特征。对40种CMH-传感器-脚手架组合进行筛选,发现一种4个核苷酸的脚手架与18个核苷酸的传感器脚手架配对的配置在测试的设计空间内表现最佳(组件级ΔΔG = -1.19 kcal/mol,在37 °C条件下)。使用针对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)S、M和L基因组片段的混合crRNA,该检测方法在三个重复实验中均检测到了最低测试输入浓度10.38 fM。在对87份来源于血浆的RNA样本进行回顾性病例对照评估中,该检测方法在47份阳性样本中的45份以及40份健康对照样本中均与RT-qPCR结果一致,得出阳性符合率为95.7%,阴性符合率为100%。通过替换crRNA,无需重新设计CMH或DNA-NS即可将识别目标转向Hantaan病毒参考RNA。本研究建立了一种模块化框架,用于无需靶标预扩增的病毒RNA拓扑结构解析检测。

full_text: Abstract Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is associated with substantial mortality, and shock with cardiac involvement is an important contributor to fatal outcomes. However, biomarker correlates, temporal trajectories, and early warning signals of clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock (CS) in SFTS remain incompletely defined. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 775 laboratory-confirmed SFTS patients admitted to Nanjing Second Hospital from April 2020 through December 2024. Time to first clinically adjudicated CS after admission was analyzed using univariable Cox regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and multivariable Cox regression. Dynamic trajectories of 6 key biomarkers over the first 14 days were assessed using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing, and restricted cubic spline models were used to characterize continuous exposure-response relationships. Results Clinically adjudicated CS occurred in 143 patients (18.5%); among 164 in-hospital deaths, 99 (60.4%) occurred in patients with CS. Elevated interleukin-6, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, urea, fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products, and triglycerides were independently associated with increased CS risk, whereas total cholesterol showed an inverse association. Most CS events clustered within the first week after admission, with approximately 85% occurring by day 7. Biomarker trajectory analyses showed sustained increases in inflammatory, cardiac, renal, and coagulation markers in patients who developed CS, whereas lipid markers showed a time-dependent decline. Conclusions In SFTS, clinically adjudicated CS clusters early after admission and reflects multisystem dysregulation involving inflammatory, cardiac, renal, coagulation, and lipid pathways. A six-biomarker panel may support early recognition of high-risk patients and help define a clinically relevant surveillance window during the first week of hospitalization, although external validation and more objective cardiac assessment are needed before routine implementation.
